column1: # The device table of the Metal backend: how large each card is, how the backend schedules work on it, and which
# timing probes work on it.
# A line that is exactly [name] starts a section; the next row is that section's header and is required as written.
# Cells are separated by one tab. No file is read at run time: the generator below runs when CMake configures.
# [devices]: one row per card. device/gen-devices.cmake compiles the rows in (device-rows.h); device/init.m reads the
# row of the card it runs on (ggml_metal_device_row_of) after its own sizing estimates, and a cell that is not - replaces
# the estimate or the default. A card with no row keeps the estimates and defaults: sizes from the name fragments in
# device/init.m when one matches, every switch off, one command buffer.
# To add a card: run any prompt on it, copy its name from the log, write the cells you measured and - for the rest, and
# say in evidence where each cell comes from (specification, measurement, estimate).
# In the on | off | - columns, - leaves the switch as it is without a row (off).
#   card: the card's name as Metal reports it, exactly: the text after "found device: " in the log of any run on that card
#       (for example: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 64). A name that differs by one character matches no card. At most 62 bytes. One row per card.
#   chip: the chip's name for the reader, printed in the log. Free text, no tab, or -.
#   architecture: the chip's architecture label for the reader (for example gcn1, gcn5, rdna1). Free text, no tab, or -.
#   wave: threads of one wave on the card, as measured (the log line "probed simd_width"), or -. For the reader: the backend probes the width itself.
#   group_bytes: bytes of threadgroup memory the card allows (MTLDevice maxThreadgroupMemoryLength), or -. For the reader: the backend asks the device.
#   cu: compute units, a number above 0, or - = keep the estimate.
#   l1_bytes_per_cu: level-1 cache per compute unit in bytes, or - = keep the estimate.
#   l2_bytes: level-2 cache in bytes, or - = keep the estimate.
#   local_Bps: memory bandwidth of the card in bytes per second, or - = keep the estimate.
#   transfer_Bps: host to card transfer bandwidth in bytes per second, or - = keep the estimate.
#   attn_gate_fuse: on | off | -. on = the attention gate's copy, sigmoid, copy and multiply run as one launch.
#   conv_l2_fold: on | off | -. on = the conv_state launch also writes the split_l2 norms of its q and k heads.
#   add_norm_fuse: on | off | -. on = a residual add, the rms norm of its sum and the weight multiply run as one launch.
#   cb_seq: command buffers after the first, encoded and committed in order on the calling thread: 0 to 8, or - = one buffer encoded as without a row.
#   set_nowait: on | off | -. on = each input upload to a discrete card is committed without waiting for it.
#   staging_keep: on | off | -. on = one logits staging buffer is kept per context and reused every token.
#   probe_dispatch: on | off | -. Counter sampling at dispatch boundaries worked on the card (probe builds only).
#   probe_stage: on | off | -. Counter sampling at stage boundaries worked (probe builds only).
#   probe_blit: on | off | -. Counter sampling at blit boundaries worked. For the reader: no code reads it.
#   probe_timestamp: on | off | -. The timestamp counter worked. A probe build samples only on a card whose row says on here.
#   evidence: where each cell or group of cells comes from: specification, measurement (with its numbers) or estimate. Free text, no tab.
